sections.title: Query
sections.text:
> As of September 2026, using only primary official documentation, identify the minimum
> reproducible checks for releasing independently installable Laravel 12-13 Composer packages from
> a monorepo: pristine consumer installation without repository-root autoload leakage,
> supported-version upgrade verification, Composer validate/install behavior, Laravel package
> auto-discovery/service-provider boot verification, semantic-versioning/BC compatibility, and
> GitHub release/tag plus split-mirror consistency. Return concise recommendations with direct
> official URLs and clearly flag anything not covered by an official source.

sections.title: Capture
sections.text:
Perplexity recommended testing tagged/dist packages from a clean consumer rather than a monorepo
checkout; running `composer validate`, locked install, strict optimized autoload and separate
`--prefer-lowest --prefer-stable` dependency resolution; executing Laravel package discovery and an
observable provider boot effect; deriving VCS versions from immutable tags rather than a manual
Composer `version`; and binding GitHub releases to their exact tags.

It explicitly classified these as project engineering controls rather than official normative
requirements: the exact temporary-directory pristine test, scanning generated Composer metadata
for monorepo paths, a Laravel 12×13 CI matrix, automated SemVer/API-diff tooling, and atomic
source-to-split provenance. P17 therefore owns those policies locally and does not attribute them to
Composer, Laravel or GitHub.

sections.title: Primary URLs returned and directly checked
Capture limitation
sections.text:
The MCP response also linked an obsolete Laravel 5.7 page; it was not used. The current Laravel 12
package documentation above was checked directly. No official source defines subtree-split atomic
publication; D97 supplies the local forward-only rule.
